breadcrumb.$comment: The way here, told in links (0054). The trail is typography, not a control: one type size of its own (a quiet line above a heading, conventionally under the body size), the gap that spaces steps and separators alike, and the link's colours — muted at rest, full strength under the pointer. The current step wears the trail's own text colour plus a weight, because under forced colours every anchor is LinkText no matter the stylesheet, and weight is the channel that survives the flattening (`req-a11y-forced-colors`). The separator rides the muted text role and is never heard: the icon host hides it on its own.
breadcrumb.$comment-link-target-min: Measured by the axe audit before it was believed: a 16px-tall link over an 8px row gap leaves a wrapped trail's touch targets 18px of safe space, and WCAG 2.5.8's inline exception covers sentences, not bars. The links take the shared floor outright (`req-a11y-touch`) — the chips' arrangement at a quieter control.
